question: What will be the closing value of the US dollar to Chinese yuan exchange rate (USDCNY=X on Yahoo Finance) on August 14, 2026?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the daily close of USDCNY=X on Yahoo Finance for 2026-08-14. If there is no close on that date (weekend or holiday), the last close before it is used.
research:
I couldn't get the official resolution value: the Yahoo Finance page and every other page I tried to open directly were blocked ("proxy refused the connection"). Everything below comes from search-result summaries. I've left out anything dated after 2026-08-04.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on Yahoo Finance USDCNY=X, daily close for 2026-08-14 (a Friday). Fetching the [history page](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/USDCNY=X/history/) failed, so **I could not confirm the latest Yahoo close.** Yahoo's close can differ by a few pips from the onshore 16:30 Beijing close.
- 2026-07-31: Exchangerates.org.uk shows USD/CNY closing at 6.7515 (range 6.7467 to 6.7553). OFX shows 6.77816, which looks like a reference or average rate, not a close. [exchangerates.org.uk](https://www.exchangerates.org.uk/USD-CNY-spot-exchange-rates-history-2026.html), [OFX](https://www.ofx.com/en-au/forex-news/historical-exchange-rates/usd/cny/)
- FRED's July 2026 monthly average is about 6.7757. [FRED EXCHUS](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/EXCHUS)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. On 2026-08-03 spot was about 6.75, roughly in the middle of the 6.65 to 6.85 range and near a 3.5-year yuan high.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-03: The yuan rose as the dollar weakened, even though the PBOC set its midpoint at 6.7898, 534 pips weaker than the Reuters estimate. Spot opened at 6.7520. The PBOC has set weaker-than-expected midpoints since November 2025, which analysts read as an effort to slow yuan gains. [Business Recorder](https://www.brecorder.com/news/40433057/yuan-firms-despite-pbocs-weaker-fixing-as-dollar-sags), [TradingView/Reuters](https://www.tradingview.com/news/reuters.com,2026:newsml_L1N44002C:0-yuan-firms-despite-pboc-s-weaker-fixing-as-dollar-sags/)
- Around 2026-07-31: The yuan touched 6.75, its strongest since February 2023, and was heading for a 7th straight weekly gain (spot about 6.7443). The midpoint was 6.7878, the strongest since 2023-02-08. Weak China July PMIs raised expectations of more policy support. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/china/currency/news/571179), [The Standard](https://www.thestandard.com.hk/finance/article/339932/Chinas-yuan-heads-for-7th-weekly-gain-on-strong-fixing-waning-US-rate-hike-hopes)
- 2026-07-30: The onshore yuan rose as much as 0.1% to 6.7550 after the dollar fell following the Fed decision. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-30/yuan-rises-to-highest-since-early-2023-as-dollar-drops-after-fed)
- 2026-07-28/29: The FOMC held rates for a fifth straight meeting. One less reliable post reports a 9-3 vote, with the three dissenters wanting a hike. [WDIY](https://www.wdiy.org/show/economic-pulse-with-dr-kamran-afshar/2026-07-31/economic-pulse-week-of-7-31-26), [Binance post](https://www.binance.com/de/square/post/350129705958034)
- 2026-07-09: Coverage of a Goldman Sachs view put USD/CNY near 6.80, with the yuan holding up against a stronger dollar. [exchangerates.org.uk](https://www.exchangerates.org.uk/news/46453/2026-07-09-usd-cny-forecast-the-yuan-is-defying-dollar-strength-goldman-sachs.html)
- Early July 2026: After a soft June jobs report, the PBOC lifted its midpoint to 6.8047, then a more-than-2-year high. [NST](https://www.nst.com.my/amp/business/economy/2026/07/1479414/chinas-yuan-inches-higher-set-first-weekly-gain-three-weeks)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- Midpoint path: 2025-11-27 at 7.0779; 2026-05-21 at 6.8349; early July about 6.80; 2026-07-31 at 6.7878; 2026-08-03 at 6.7898. [investingLive Nov](https://investinglive.com/centralbank/pboc-sets-usd-cny-mid-point-today-at-70779-vs-estimate-at-70733-20251127/), [investingLive May](https://investinglive.com/centralbank/pboc-sets-usd-cny-mid-point-today-at-68349-vs-estimate-at-67955-20260521/)
- The trend is a steady fall in USD/CNY (a stronger yuan) of about 0.03 to 0.04 per month in 2026. Spot moved from about 6.80 in early July to about 6.75 by the end of July, roughly -0.05 in a month.
- The midpoint sits about 0.03 to 0.04 weaker (higher USD/CNY) than spot. The PBOC is slowing the gains rather than reversing them. Spot can trade within ±2% of the midpoint.
- Typical variation, my own rough estimate and not from a source: USD/CNY usually has annualized volatility of about 3 to 4%, which works out to a one-standard-deviation move of about ±0.03 to 0.05 CNY over the 8 trading days to August 14. Weekly moves of more than 0.1 have been rare in 2026.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on USD/CNY.
- 2026-05-12: Goldman Sachs forecast 6.80 in 3 months, 6.70 in 6 months and 6.50 in 12 months, calling the yuan about 20% undervalued. [investingLive](https://investinglive.com/forex/goldman-sachs-says-yuan-20-undervalued-lifts-forecasts-to-650-in-a-year-20260512/)
- Analysts expect a "rise then stabilize" path for 2026, with a core range of 6.6 to 7.0. An aggregator cites a 19-bank consensus year-end target of 6.90, but it is undated and probably stale. [BigGo](https://finance.biggo.com/news/b69332c3-0cb0-44ce-a366-7eb2c64382cf), [fxbankforecast](https://fxbankforecast.com/reports/goldman/currencies/CNY)

## 6. Upcoming events before August 14
These are typical release dates; I did not verify them.
- About 2026-08-07: US July jobs report. Soft US data has been the main trigger for yuan gains in June and July.
- About 2026-08-07: China July trade data. About 2026-08-09/10: China July CPI and PPI.
- About 2026-08-12/13: US July CPI and PPI, which feed into Fed expectations. The market has been weighing a hike against a hold.
- About 2026-08-14: China July activity data (industrial output, retail sales). It may come out on the 14th or the 15th.
- Every day: the PBOC midpoint. A bigger gap below the Reuters estimate would be a stronger signal of pushback against yuan gains. Also relevant are US-China trade or tariff headlines and the broad dollar (DXY), for which I found no recent level.
